name: Imidapril
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 5 to 10 mg once daily; start 2.5 mg in severe hypertension, kidney impairment or renal parenchymal hypertension

key_interactions.action: Contraindicated unless blood pressure is markedly uncontrolled.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: AN69 dialysis membranes; dextran sulfate LDL apheresis
Potassium-sparing diuretics, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, potassium supplements, salt substitutes, trimethoprim

key_interactions.effect: Acute kidney injury; less blood-pressure effect.

contraindications: History of angioedema (ACE inhibitor, hereditary, acquired or idiopathic)
AN69 hemodialysis; dextran sulfate or similar apheresis

pk.excretion_renal_pct: Urinary (reduced in kidney impairment); percentage not stated

sources.citation: Ministry of Health Singapore. (2026). Tanatril tablets 10 mg (imidapril hydrochloride) [SIN10614P; National Drug Formulary product information; last updated October 9, 2026].

Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) CKD Work Group. (2024). KDIGO 2024 clinical practice guideline for the evaluation and management of chronic kidney disease. Kidney International, 105(4S), S117–S314.
